summary.text: An adult cochlear implant recipient was implanted with a MED-EL Concerto Flex28 in 2012. FNS began 2 months after initial activation and progressed, with speech scores declining and loudness limited to soft. Biphasic and triphasic stimulation with monopolar grounding did not help, and the implant was confirmed to function within normal limits on manufacturer integrity testing.

Temporary paralysis of the facial nerve eye branches with local anesthetic allowed adequate loudness without FNS and unchanged auditory thresholds, after which a decision was made to trial the Neuro Zti device. The patient was reimplanted with the Neuro Zti EVO electrode by a round window approach. Intraoperative testing showed FNS with stimulus MB on 12 electrodes and none with stimulus MMA.

Two extra-cochlear electrodes were deactivated and five more for poor auditory perception. Postoperative loudness growth showed FNS at soft levels with stimulus MB and no FNS with MMA, reaching only medium loudness. Speech scores improved over the pre-reimplantation scores, and no FNS has been reported beyond 1.5 years after activation, though best scores were with the original implant.

summary.text: An adult cochlear implant recipient with meningitis as the listed aetiology was implanted with a Cochlear CI22 M in 1995. FNS developed after 13 years of CI use and progressed, with speech recognition deteriorating. Grounding configuration changes altered current requirements but FNS remained problematic in all conditions, and a one-week break did not change the FN threshold or loudness.

Reimplantation with the Neuro Zti device was offered and the patient was reimplanted with the Neuro Zti EVO electrode by a round window approach, leaving seven extra-cochlear electrodes. Intraoperative testing showed an FN response with stimulus MB on one electrode and none with stimulus MMA. Ten of 20 electrodes were later deactivated, seven extra-cochlear at surgery and three apparently extruded.

Postoperative loudness growth reached a loud percept without FNS with both stimulus types. At 7 weeks BKB scores were 50% for the male speaker and 78% for the female speaker. The patient had difficulty adapting to the new sound but reported acclimatization over time, and no FNS has been reported with clinical MAPs to date.

summary.text: An adult cochlear implant recipient with ototoxicity and possible dehiscence listed as aetiology was implanted with a MED-EL Synchrony Flex28 in August 2019. FNS occurred on activation, no break was given, and biphasic and triphasic stimulation with monopolar grounding did not improve FNS or hearing. The patient was never able to understand speech with the CI alone.

Reimplantation with the Neuro Zti CI was offered and performed with the EVO electrode by a round window approach, giving a full insertion. Intraoperative testing showed FNS with stimulus MB on all 20 electrodes and none with stimulus MMA. No electrodes needed deactivation.

Postoperative loudness growth showed FNS below auditory threshold with stimulus MB, while loud levels were reached with stimulus MMA without FNS. At 4 months speech scores were 62% BKB male speaker, 24% BKB female speaker and 78% CUNY, the first speech testing completed with a CI. No FNS has been reported with clinical MAPs to date.

article_limitations: Three supplementary DOCX files (supplementary tables 1 and 2, supplementary figures 1 and 2 are cited in the text) are listed as figures s001 to s003 with no caption and no resolved URL, and the source declares no supplements; their content was not reviewed.

Cohort-level statements without an explicit all-patient wording (for example activation 2 to 6 weeks after surgery, electrode position confirmed by postoperative X-ray, programming limited loudness) are not copied to individual patients.
Values printed inside Figure 2 are pixel content recorded only in visual.json; no estimated plot values are recorded.
Patient sex and exact ages are not stated; the series reports adults only.
Discussion of a single control sample reimplanted with the same device cites supplementary table 2 and is not a patient of this series.
The Methods count of five electrodes tested for patient 1 conflicts with 12 of 16 in Table 2; patient 2 has 13 versus 14 electrodes tested.

Discussion sentence "All patients achieved adequate volume percept without FNS for stimulus MMA" is a study-level conclusion and is not copied; it is not treated as a conflict with patient 1 reaching only "medium" loudness on single-electrode testing, because "adequate" is not a loudness rating and MCL was reached for all active electrodes in routine programming.

Discussion sentence "none of the presented patients have experienced FNS since reimplantation" refers to clinical use; patient 1 and 3 FNS with stimulus MB during postoperative loudness testing is recorded per patient and the cohort sentence is not copied.
The Table 2 "Full Insertion (Yr)" years are not attached to the reimplant events because the header does not state which event the year dates.
